memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now then, just as the Lord promised, he has kept me alive for forty-five years since the time he said this to Moses, while Israel moved about in the wilderness. So here I am today, eighty-five years old! I am still as strong today as the day Moses sent me out; I'm just as vigorous to go out to battle now as I was then" - Josh 14:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Caleb is eighty-five years old, and he is not asking for a quiet retirement. He testifies that God has kept him alive through forty-five years, and that he is as strong now as the day he was sent out. Far from winding down, Caleb is ready for one more battle. His faith has not aged even if his body has walked many miles.

The first thing Caleb credits is God's faithfulness: "the Lord... has kept me alive." He does not boast in his own hardiness as though his strength were self-made. Every one of those forty-five years was a gift, a sign of God's sustaining hand. Caleb's vigour was, at root, God's grace to him.

There is real encouragement here for anyone who feels their best years are behind them. God is not done with people simply because they have grown older. Caleb's most famous act of faith came at eighty-five. Scripture promises that those planted in the house of the Lord still bear fruit in old age, staying fresh and green (Ps 92:14). Whatever your age, God can still use you, still strengthen you, still call you forward. Our outer self may be wasting away, but the God who renews us inwardly day by day is not finished (2 Cor 4:16).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you believe God can still use you meaningfully, whatever your age?
- To whom do you give credit for the strength and years you have?
- What "one more battle" might God still be calling you toward?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for every year You have given me and every measure of strength. Whatever my age, keep me useful in Your hands and fruitful for Your glory. Amen.
